Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

confession noun

an admission

also admission, own up, admit, I have a confession to make

classical

Cic. Div. 1.33 (Lewis & Short: errātī suī)
Liv. 21.18.5 (Lewis & Short: culpae)
Quint. 6.3.9

cōnfessiō, cōnfessiōnis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

an admission, an acknowledgment

An admission of a fault or of anything else, with the genitive of what is admitted.

Other words

  • cōnfiteor, cōnfitērī, cōnfessus sum — admit, own up

    verb, second conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Mart. 4.49.10: cōnfiteor: laudant illa, sed ista legunt · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    The verb: to admit, own up; in the Church also to confess sins and to praise God.

Examples

  • nec vultūs modo ac vōcis exprimit cōnfessiōnem, sed tōtum corpus vī suā concutit

    laughter forces a confession not only from the face and voice, but shakes the whole bodyQuint. 6.3.9

  • Sī rem ipsam ingenuē cōnfiteāre, forsitan dēlictī grātiam faciet.

    If you just own up frankly, perhaps he’ll let you off.Pont. Progymn. 1.4

See also confession, I’m sorry, I apologise.
